# `bom_multi_level`

**Tier 2** — canonical — the only tier humans edit · owned by `data-ingestion` · `public.bom_multi_level`

**One row is** One child-to-parent line of a deep bill of materials: this material is consumed by this higher-level component, at this level of the tree. Collapsed to effective product-to-material arcs before the engine sees it. UNIQUE on `natural_key_intended` since WP 3.3 (`20260916000018`), and the index is NULLS NOT DISTINCT because a ROOT line has no parent — without that clause the constraint would hold every line except the roots (D5 closed).

**Natural key:** `project_id` + `plant_name` + `material_id` + `higher_level_component_id` + `level` — the key this table's grain implies, and the
database ENFORCES it: `bom_multi_level_natural_key`. A re-upload of the same row updates
it rather than duplicating it.

`write` names the capability that exists today. WP 2.2 splits `data_editing` into `data_edit_inputs` (tier 2) and `data_edit_policies` (tier 4); this row becomes `data_edit_inputs` then, and all twelve sidecars change together.

> **What the database actually permits is wider than the row above.**
> 2 policies here grant access with
> **no predicate at all** (`USING (true)`), so the capability named above is what the
> product intends to check, not what the database enforces:
>
> - `bom_multi_level_auth_read` — `SELECT` to `authenticated`
> - `bom_multi_level_anon_read` — `SELECT` to `anon`
>
> See PLAN.md D28: the application runs as the
> `anon` role with no auth session and the anon key ships in the frontend bundle, so
> closing these is a migration with an auth model behind it rather than a policy edit.

**Resolution** — how a value is decided when more than one source could supply one.

| | |
|---|---|
| Default mode | `asserted` |
| Assertable by | `csv_upload` |
| Estimable from | **never** — this value may not be estimated |
| Hybrid (centre / spread) | **none** — the engine has no variability field for this quantity |
| On conflict | `assertion_wins` |

estimable_from is EMPTY and that is a positive statement, not an omission. This is an engineering or commercial fact that someone knows exactly — it is written on a drawing, in a contract, or on a machine's nameplate. Fitting a distribution to it would produce a number with error bars around something that has no error, and the error bars would be believed. A future estimator reading this contract must refuse this field. Same rule as bom_single_level.consumption_rate, and more important here: multi-level rates multiply down the tree, so an estimate at level 3 propagates into every product above it.
